industries.warehouse.title: Warehouse robots: AMR, pallets | Professional Robotics
industries.warehouse.description: Warehouse robotics without stopping the warehouse: pallet-handling robots, AMRs for order picking, palletizing and sorting. Start with one route.
industries.warehouse.name: Warehousing and logistics
industries.warehouse.lead: A warehouse is a flow: pallets arrive, goods are picked into orders, orders leave. Robots take over moving and repetitive operations; people stay where a decision or an oversized load is involved.
industries.warehouse.lead2: It is better to start with one route than with the whole warehouse: the effect shows quickly and the investment stays small.

industries.warehouse.problems.items.0.te: In developed economies there are 500–800 robots per 10,000 employees; Russia’s target for 2030 is 145. Only 3% of surveyed companies had fully automated warehouses.
industries.warehouse.problems.items.1.ti: Labor shortage eased, pay did not.
industries.warehouse.problems.items.1.te: In 2025, 65% of surveyed companies named the labor shortage as a problem. By 2026, labor market tension fell to 0.04–0.09 vacancies per 1,000 m².

Pallet-handling robots and AMRs move pallets horizontally: dock, rack, shipping zone. The simplest entry point: the route is clear and the warehouse is not rebuilt.
Borjomi plans to hand all horizontal movements to robots
An AMR works on the goods-to-person scheme: the rack comes to the worker, not the other way round. Or it follows the picker and carries what has been picked.
picker output at Magnit: from about 18 to over 32 tons
A robotic arm unloads cartons from a pallet or builds a pallet for shipping. Heavy, monotonous work leaves the dock.

industries.warehouse.pilot.items.0.title: Site assessment
industries.warehouse.pilot.items.0.text: We look at flows, aisle widths, floor surface, thresholds and docks. We choose the route where a robot pays off soonest.
industries.warehouse.pilot.items.1.title: One route
industries.warehouse.pilot.items.1.text: The robot runs one route under your normal load, without stopping the warehouse. Tasks come from your WMS or 1C.
industries.warehouse.pilot.items.2.title: Review and decision
industries.warehouse.pilot.items.2.text: We compare distance walked, speed and errors before and after. Then we decide which routes and operations to move to robots next.
industries.warehouse.vendorsLead: We select equipment for the load, aisle width and floor surface, not from a catalog. Robots from different brands work in one system.
industries.warehouse.why.title: Different brands, one window.
industries.warehouse.why.text: AMRs and pallet-handling robots from different manufacturers appear in one window: routes, tasks and reports. Tasks come from your WMS or 1C, and we maintain the fleet under an SLA.
